pages.title: Authentication (https://developer.monday.com/api-reference/docs/authentication)
pages.text:
Authentication For AI agents: the docs index is at https://developer.monday.com/api-reference/llms.txt. The index for every project on this site is at https://developer.monday.com/llms.txt. Append .md to any documentation page URL to get its markdown version. The monday.com platform API utilizes personal V2 API tokens to authenticate requests and identify the user making the call. These tokens are unique to each user and have no explicit length. Personal tokens allow you to interact with the API using your own user account. Their permissions mirror what you can do in the monday.com UI, ensuring that API access is consistent with your platform-level permissions. If you don't have a monday.com account yet, create a free developer account to get an API token and start testing. Token permissions Personal tokens mirror all permission levels set in the monday.com UI, including board , column , item , or account access. For example: If you don't have permission to access a certain workspace via the UI, you won't have permission using your personal API token either. App tokens have an additional set of permission scopes that specify which queries and mutations it can access, while personal tokens have all permission scopes. Accessing your token You can access your API token in two ways, depending on your user type . In the Developer Center (all users) All users with API access can follow these steps to access their API token: In your monday.com account, click on your profile picture in the top right corner. Select Developers . This will open the Developer Center in another tab. Click API token > Show . Copy your personal token. In the Administration tab (account admins only) Account admins can use the Developer Center steps above or access their token via the Administration tab: In your monday.com account, click on your profile picture in the top right corner. Select Administration > Connections > Personal API token . Copy your personal token. Making requests with your token Once you have your token, you can make requests with the API by passing the token in the Authorization header. cURL curl -X POST https://api.monday.com/v2 \
  -H "Authorization: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "query { me { id name } }"}' Regenerating a token API tokens can be regenerated at any time. However, this will immediately invalidate your current token, so be sure to update any integrations using it. How to regenerate a token In the Developer Center In your monday.com account, click on your profile picture in the top right corner. Select Developers . This will open the Developer Center in another tab. Click API token > Regenerate . In the Administration tab In your monday.com account, click on your profile picture in the top right corner. Select Administration > Connections > Personal API token . Click Regenerate . Updated about 2 months ago Did this page help you? Yes No Copy Page

pages.text: Get started with monday MCP – Support How can we help you? Get started with monday MCP Connect & automate 2 min read monday MCP is the hosted server that gives AI tools secure access to your monday.com workspace. It connects your account directly to AI assistants like Claude, Cursor, and Copilot Studio through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard for AI integrations. Prerequisites An active monday.com account with appropriate permissions MCP is preinstalled on all monday.com accounts. If you can't connect, ask your admin to check Admin → Permissions → AI Connectors . See Managing AI Connectors & MCP Access for more information. Supported AI client OAuth consent for monday MCP when prompted by your client What can you do with monday MCP? Project reporting – generate sprint summaries, team performance reports, and deadline tracking from your boards (including monday dev sprints) Smart task management – convert meeting notes into structured items, assign tasks, and update statuses through natural language Cross-team visibility – ask for rollups like “What’s blocking the launch?” across Product, Marketing, and RevOps boards Operational workflows – create and triage incidents, support requests, and ops checklists (with clear owners, priority, and due dates) CRM workflows – create leads and deals, update pipeline stages, and log next steps from call notes Docs + knowledge workflows – create specs, SOPs, and retros as monday docs (in a workspace or attached to an item) Dashboards & insights – build dashboards and widgets, and answer questions using board insights (such as status distribution, workload, and throughput) Workspace discovery – quickly find the right board, doc, form, or folder, even in large workspaces Key use cases Quick data retrieval – ask for board status, find items, or summarize what changed this week Task creation and cleanup – turn a meeting transcript into tasks with owners, priority, and due dates Updating existing work – update status, people, or date fields when plans change, with human review before applying changes Cross-board analysis – ask questions like “What’s overdue across all launch boards?” or “Which team has the most blockers?” Executive reporting – create weekly rollups such as shipped vs. planned, scope changes, and risk summaries Support and Service operations – intake requests, link relevant context, and keep stakeholders updated through item updates Documentation workflows – generate a spec in monday docs and attach it to the relevant initiative item Automation-style chains – run multi-step flows like “Create a bug, assign it, set severity, and notify the team in an update” Note: Other tools that support the Model Context Protocol should also be compatible, though individual setup steps may vary Available tools Please check out the Available tools article for a full list. FAQs Pricing and availability Is MCP included in my monday.com plan? Yes. MCP is available on all monday.com plans at no additional cost. Are there usage limits? Standard API limits apply. Security and privacy What permissions does MCP have? Each user individually authorizes MCP via OAuth. MCP only has access to the data that you, as an individual user, can access in monday.com. The specific permissions depend on the OAuth scopes you grant during setup. Is my data secure? Yes. MCP uses industry-standard OAuth for authentication and TLS encryption for all data transfers. MCP respects your monday.com permissions, meaning you can only access or modify data you’re authorized to change. Because MCP can perform actions on your behalf, we recommend reviewing AI-suggested changes before confirming actions that modify your workspace. Who can see my data? Only you and your AI assistant can see the data exchanged through MCP. monday.com does not review or access the content of your conversations. If you have any questions, please reach out to our team right here . We’re available 24/7 and happy to help.
